title: Improve API error responses with consistent error schema
body:
## Description

Standardize error responses across all API endpoints using a Pydantic error model with code, message, and details fields.

## Context

Currently, error responses may vary in structure across endpoints, making it harder for API consumers to handle errors programmatically. A consistent error schema simplifies client-side error handling.

## Proposed Error Schema

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "INVALID_INPUT",
    "message": "The provided network flow data is missing required fields",
    "details": [
      {"field": "src_port", "issue": "Field is required"},
      {"field": "protocol", "issue": "Must be one of: TCP, UDP, ICMP"}
    ],
    "request_id": "abc-123"
  }
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Create a Pydantic `ErrorResponse` model with code, message, and details
- [ ] Define error code constants (INVALID_INPUT, NOT_FOUND, ENGINE_ERROR, etc.)
- [ ] Add custom exception handlers for FastAPI
- [ ] Refactor all endpoints to use the consistent error schema
- [ ] Include a unique request_id in error responses for tracing
- [ ] Add unit tests verifying error response format for various error types
- [ ] Document the error schema in API documentation

title: Add health check endpoint to FastAPI
body:
## Description

Add a `GET /health` endpoint that returns the status of all 4 detection engines (loaded/not loaded) and database connectivity.

## Context

Health check endpoints are essential for container orchestration (Docker, Kubernetes), load balancers, and monitoring systems. The endpoint should provide a quick overview of system readiness.

## Expected Response

```json
{
  "status": "healthy",
  "engines": {
    "anomaly_detection": {"status": "loaded", "model_version": "v1.2"},
    "signature_detection": {"status": "loaded", "rules_count": 450},
    "behavioral_analysis": {"status": "loaded", "profiles_count": 12},
    "threat_intelligence": {"status": "loaded", "iocs_count": 8900}
  },
  "database": {"status": "connected", "latency_ms": 2},
  "uptime_seconds": 3600,
  "timestamp": "2026-03-01T12:00:00Z"
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Add `GET /health` endpoint to FastAPI router
- [ ] Check and report status of all 4 detection engines
- [ ] Check database connectivity with a simple query
- [ ] Return HTTP 200 when healthy, HTTP 503 when any critical component is down
- [ ] Include uptime and timestamp in response
- [ ] Add unit tests for healthy and degraded states
- [ ] Keep endpoint lightweight (no expensive operations)

title: Add --dry-run mode to main.py
body:
## Description

Add a `--dry-run` flag to `main.py` that runs the feature extraction and detection pipeline without requiring Scapy packet capture (no root required). Use a sample PCAP file or synthetic data instead.

## Context

Currently, running the detector requires root privileges for Scapy packet capture. This makes development and testing inconvenient. A dry-run mode would allow developers to test the full pipeline without root access or a live network.

## Expected Behavior

```bash
# Instead of: sudo python main.py
python main.py --dry-run                        # Uses built-in synthetic data
python main.py --dry-run --input sample.pcap    # Uses a PCAP file
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Add `--dry-run` CLI flag using argparse
- [ ] In dry-run mode, skip Scapy live capture
- [ ] Generate synthetic network data or load from a bundled sample PCAP
- [ ] Run the full detection pipeline (feature extraction, ML model, rule engine)
- [ ] Output results in the same format as live mode
- [ ] Add a small sample PCAP file or synthetic data generator for testing
- [ ] Update README with dry-run usage instructions
- [ ] Add tests verifying dry-run mode works end-to-end

title: Add unit tests for rule engine pattern matching
body:
## Description

The rule engine uses regex patterns for detecting SQL injection, XSS, and other attack patterns. Add targeted unit tests for each pattern to ensure detection accuracy.

## Context

The rule-based detection component is critical for catching known attack patterns. Without thorough tests, regex pattern changes could silently break detection or introduce false positives.

## Test Cases to Add

- **SQL Injection:** UNION SELECT, OR 1=1, DROP TABLE, comment injection (--)
- **XSS:** Script tags, event handlers (onload, onerror), javascript: URIs
- **Command Injection:** Pipe operators, backticks, semicolons in payloads
- **Path Traversal:** ../ sequences, null bytes, encoded traversal
- **False positives:** Benign strings that should NOT trigger patterns

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Add `tests/test_rule_engine.py` with tests for each attack pattern category
- [ ] Include at least 3 positive matches and 2 false-positive checks per pattern
- [ ] Test pattern matching is case-insensitive where appropriate
- [ ] Test URL-encoded and double-encoded variants
- [ ] All tests pass with `pytest`
- [ ] Document each test case with a brief description of what it validates

title: Add word count and reading time to generated reports
body:
## Description

Add metadata at the top of generated research reports showing word count and estimated reading time.

## Context

Research reports can vary significantly in length. Adding word count and reading time helps users quickly assess a report's scope and plan their time. This is a common feature in blogs and documentation platforms.

## Expected Output

At the top of each generated report:
```
Word count: 2,450 | Estimated reading time: 10 min
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Calculate word count of the generated report content
- [ ] Estimate reading time based on average reading speed (200-250 words/minute)
- [ ] Add metadata line at the top of the report (after title, before content)
- [ ] Include metadata in both the Streamlit UI display and any exported files
- [ ] Add unit tests for word count and reading time calculation
- [ ] Handle edge cases: empty reports, reports with code blocks, reports with tables

title: Add research source for Google Scholar
body:
## Description

Add a new research tool that searches Google Scholar for academic papers, following the existing pattern in `research_tools.py`.

## Context

The Research Agent currently uses web search tools but lacks a dedicated academic paper search. Google Scholar is the most widely used academic search engine and would significantly improve research quality for scientific topics.

## Suggested Approach

- Use the `scholarly` Python package or SerpAPI's Google Scholar endpoint
- Follow the existing tool pattern in `research_tools.py` (same interface/structure)
- Return title, authors, year, citation count, abstract snippet, and URL
- Add rate limiting to respect Google Scholar's usage policies

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Add Google Scholar search function in `research_tools.py`
- [ ] Follow the existing tool interface pattern for consistency
- [ ] Return structured results: title, authors, year, citation count, abstract, URL
- [ ] Add rate limiting (max 1 request per 2 seconds)
- [ ] Handle cases where Scholar returns no results gracefully
- [ ] Add unit tests with mocked responses
- [ ] Add `scholarly` (or chosen library) to requirements
- [ ] Update README with the new research source

title: Add pagination to GET /api/alerts endpoint
body:
## Description

The `GET /api/alerts` endpoint currently returns all alerts without pagination. Add limit/offset pagination with proper response headers.

## Context

As the system runs, the alerts table grows continuously. Returning all alerts in a single response becomes slow and memory-intensive. Pagination is essential for production use.

## Expected Behavior

**Request:**
```
GET /api/alerts?limit=20&offset=0
```

**Response headers:**
```
X-Total-Count: 1523
X-Page-Size: 20
X-Page-Offset: 0
```

**Response body:**
```json
{
  "alerts": [...],
  "total": 1523,
  "limit": 20,
  "offset": 0
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Add `limit` and `offset` query parameters to `GET /api/alerts`
- [ ] Default limit to 20, max limit to 100
- [ ] Return total count in response body and `X-Total-Count` header
- [ ] Use efficient SQL query with LIMIT/OFFSET
- [ ] Return 400 for invalid pagination parameters (negative, non-integer)
- [ ] Add unit tests for pagination (first page, middle page, last page, invalid params)
- [ ] Maintain backward compatibility (no params = first page with default limit)

title: Add API endpoint for model performance metrics
body:
## Description

Add a `GET /api/model/metrics` endpoint that returns precision, recall, and F1-score of the currently active ML model.

## Context

Operators need visibility into how well the active model is performing. Exposing model metrics via the API enables monitoring dashboards and automated alerting on model degradation.

## Expected Response

```json
{
  "model_name": "random_forest_v2",
  "metrics": {
    "precision": 0.95,
    "recall": 0.92,
    "f1_score": 0.93,
    "accuracy": 0.94
  },
  "evaluated_at": "2026-03-01T12:00:00Z",
  "sample_count": 10000
}
```

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Add `GET /api/model/metrics` endpoint to FastAPI router
- [ ] Return precision, recall, F1-score, and accuracy from the active model
- [ ] Include model name/version and evaluation timestamp
- [ ] Cache metrics to avoid recomputation on every request
- [ ] Return 503 if no model is loaded
- [ ] Add unit tests for the endpoint (model loaded and not loaded cases)
- [ ] Add the endpoint to API documentation

- [ ] Return validation error messages in Spanish when `Accept-Language: es` is set
- [ ] Default to English when no language header is provided
- [ ] Add tests for both English and Spanish error responses
- [ ] Update API documentation with the new header support

| Tool | Has README | Has Tests |
|------|-----------|-----------|
| `account_info_tool` | ✅ | ❌ |

| `hubspot_tool` | ❌ | ❌ |
| `intercom_tool` | ✅ | ❌ |
| `port_scanner` | ✅ | ❌ |
| `risk_scorer` | ✅ | ❌ |
| `ssl_tls_scanner` | ✅ | ❌ |
| `subdomain_enumerator` | ✅ | ❌ |
| `tech_stack_detector` | ✅ | ❌ |

**Note:** `test_security_tools.py` exists with some coverage for cookie analysis and port checking, but dedicated test files per tool would improve coverage and maintainability.

## Why This Matters

- Security tools need thorough testing
- API integration tools (brevo, hubspot, intercom) need validation tests
- Individual test files make CI failures easier to debug
- Helps catch regressions

## Proposed Solution

Create test files following the existing pattern (e.g., `test_gmail_tool.py`, `test_google_analytics_tool.py`):

Each should test:
- Input validation
- Error handling (missing credentials, API errors)
- Core functionality with mocked HTTP responses
- Credential retrieval from store and environment

Happy to implement if assigned.
